summary:
VALMED – Astronaut Health Monitoring and Support System

VALMED is a web-based health monitoring prototype designed to support astronaut well-being during long-duration space missions. It brings together crew health check-ins, longitudinal health trends, symptom tracking, interactive 3D anatomy, structured symptom protocols, and mission hazard awareness in one integrated platform.

The system uses a deterministic, explainable assessment engine to review available health observations, identify changes that may require attention, and distinguish missing or outdated data from current measurements. Its interactive anatomy viewer connects reported symptoms to relevant body structures, while its hazard module explores NASA’s five human spaceflight hazard domains.

VALMED also includes a 150-day synthetic lunar mission scenario to demonstrate how health indicators and mission events can be explored over time. An optional AI assistant runs locally through Ollama, while deterministic safety protocols remain authoritative.

VALMED aims to make astronaut health information more understandable, connected, and actionable while clearly communicating its scientific and medical limitations.
details:
VALMED is an astronaut health monitoring and support platform designed to address the challenges of maintaining crew health during long-duration space missions.

The platform integrates health check-ins, physiological data tracking, longitudinal trends, symptom reporting, interactive 3D human anatomy, spaceflight hazard monitoring, and structured medical support protocols into a unified interface.

Its deterministic assessment engine analyzes available health observations, identifies potentially concerning changes, and distinguishes between missing, outdated, and recorded measurements. The system also includes a 150-day simulated lunar mission, demonstrating how astronaut health indicators and environmental conditions can evolve throughout an extended mission.

VALMED incorporates an interactive 3D anatomy viewer that connects reported symptoms with relevant body structures, alongside a module addressing NASA’s five human spaceflight hazards. An optional AI-powered assistant runs locally using Ollama, helping users understand health information while deterministic safety protocols remain independent of AI-generated responses.

The project was developed using JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Three.js, Node.js, and Ollama. Its design combines scientific visualization, interactive 3D environments, and an intuitive mission-control interface.

VALMED’s intended impact is to make astronaut health information more accessible, understandable, and actionable, supporting earlier recognition of potential health concerns and better-informed decisions during missions where access to Earth-based medical assistance may be limited.

The project prioritizes explainability, data traceability, privacy, accessibility, and scientific honesty. It is a research and demonstration prototype, not a clinically validated medical device.
